title: Current watches, warnings, and advisories

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 28 at 11:20AM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
At 1120 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Salisbury University, moving east at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph, heavy rain, and frequent
lightning.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Reduced visibility and minor flooding
possible. Frequent cloud to ground lightning strikes.

This strong thunderstorm will be near...
Salisbury, Fruitland, and Salisbury University around 1125 AM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this storm include Salisbury-Wicomico,
Pittsville, Chesapeake Heights, Powellville, Melson, Whiton, Shad
Point, Willards, and Lakewood.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued August 28 at 8:18AM PDT until August 29 at 3:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hazardous sea conditions.

* WHERE...East Santa Barbara Channel from Pt. Conception to Pt.
Mugu CA including Santa Cruz Island.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 3 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...See the Coastal Waters Forecast (CWFLOX)
for more.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 28 at 10:18AM CDT until August 28 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Randall County in the panhandle of Texas...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1018 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Amarillo, Canyon and Mescalero Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 28 at 11:12AM EDT until August 28 at 12:15PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
SMWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly NJ has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Delaware Bay...

* Until 1215 PM EDT.

* At 1109 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located near Fourteen
Foot Bank Light, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Miah Maull Light, Brandywine Shoal Light, Fourteen Foot Bank Light,
and East Point.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 28 at 9:43AM CDT until August 31 at 2:00PM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Illinois...

Wabash River from Hutsonville to Vincennes.

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crest. Flooding should come to an end on
the Wabash during the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Extensive flooding is in progress.  Higher
rural roads begin to flood.  High water isolates many river cabins.
Seep water becomes a problem.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM CDT /10:00 AM EDT/ Friday the stage was 19.4 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:00 AM CDT /10:00 AM EDT/ Friday was 20.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Monday morning and continue falling to 5.0 feet Monday, September
07.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 945 PM CDT /1045 PM
EDT/.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued August 28 at 6:37AM AKDT until August 28 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50
mph expected, mainly near the coast.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Western Capes, and Northern Bristol Bay
Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gusty onshore winds continue this morning and
will slowly decrease through this afternoon. With a long fetch of
high end small craft and gale force winds, this will result in
higher waves and rough seas along the Kuskokwim Bay coast. Even
though winds are expected to slowly decrease late this morning into
this afternoon, high seas coinciding with high tide this afternoon
will likely push water levels 1 to 2 feet above the normal high
tide line for the Kuskokwim Bay coast.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 28 at 10:28AM AST until August 28 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

line.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued August 28 at 6:10AM AKDT until August 29 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 6
inches at or above pass level. Wind gusts up to 30 mph. Blowing
snow could reduce visibility to 1/2 mile or less at times. Pockets
of wintry mix possible.

* WHERE...Central Brooks Range, primarily Atigun Pass.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow is initially expected above 2500 feet,
with snow levels rising to 4000 feet Friday afternoon. What snow
does fall is expected to be wet and have difficulty blowing.
Blowing snow is most likely above 4000 feet.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 28 at 6:51AM PDT until August 28 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 3 PM PDT THIS AFTERNOON
DUE TO LIGHTNING FOR SANTA CRUZ MOUNTAINS, SOUTHERN SALINAS
VALLEY/ARROYO SECO AND LAKE SAN ANTONIO, SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND
LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST, NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY/HOLLISTER VALLEY
AND CARMEL VALLEY, NORTHERN MONTEREY BAY, AND SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY
AND BIG SUR COAST...

....The potential for isolated thunderstorms across the Central Coast
continues from this morning through Friday afternoon...

* AFFECTED AREA...The Salinas and Carmel Valleys and Hollister Area,
Monterey Bay and the Big Sur Coast, The Santa Cruz Mountains, and
Interior Monterey County and the Santa Lucia Range.

* TIMING...Until 3 PM PDT this afternoon.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Lightning strikes with little precipitation and
gusty and erratic outflow winds of 40 to 50 mph.

* IMPACTS...There will be an increased risk for power outages.
Lightning strikes may result in new fire ignitions. Erratic outflow
winds will result in rapid fire spread for both new and existing
fires.
properties.instruction:
Please advise responding agencies or fire crews in the field of this
fire weather alert.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How
will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you
call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more
information.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 28 at 9:17AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
ESFSJU

The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical Storm
Dolly, located nearly 1200 miles southeast of the local islands. The
official forecast calls for Dolly to degenerate into a tropical wave
before reaching the area on Sunday and Monday.

Since the system is expected to find a hostile environment, a
widespread and long-lasting rainfall event is not anticipated.
Instead, squally weather will bring periods of moderate to locally
heavy rainfall, beginning late Sunday and stretching into Monday. In
general, we are anticipating rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches,
which will be beneficial for any areas receiving the rain. Lingering
moisture from the remnants of Dolly could contribute to additional
showers developing on Tuesday. The risk of flooding is low to locally
medium. Areas with the drainage system clogged by death vegetation
debris or urbanized areas with poor drainage could experience
localized flooding.

Any rainfall will be welcome, and could bring a temporary relieve to
the ongoing severe to extreme drought plaguing Puerto Rico and the
Virgin Islands. However, the rain should not be enough to end the
drought.

At this time, the confidence in the forecast is medium, and the users
are advised to monitor the forecast in case changes are introduced.
If that the case, this product will be update accordingly.

NWSheadline: Beneficial rains from the remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly are expected to reach Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands on Sunday and Monday

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 28 at 5:03AM PDT until August 28 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures of 95 to 100.

* WHERE...Orange County Inland Areas.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Low temperatures 5 to 10 degrees above normal
will limit overnight relief from the heat and will increase the
threat of heat-related illness.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 28 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for today. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: CODE ORANGE OZONE FORECAST FOR TODAY
